messages.text: London misses out as Nairobi secures 2029 World Athletics Championships

metadata.summary: The World Athletics Championships are heading to Africa for the first time after Kenya's capital Nairobi was confirmed as host of the 2029 edition, with London missing out.
metadata.content: World Athletics Championships: London misses out as Nairobi secures 2029 event | 'We are deeply disappointed' | Sky Sports Skip to content World Athletics Championships: London misses out as Nairobi secures 2029 event | 'We are deeply disappointed' The 2029 World Athletics Championships will be held in Nairobi, Kenya; it will be the first time the event has taken place in Africa; London's bid was unsuccessful, with UK Athletics CEO Jack Buckner saying: "We had an outstanding bid which would genuinely take the sport to new levels" Tuesday 15 September 2026 15:56, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player World Athletics President Lord Coe explains why they have awarded the World Championships to Nairobi and Munich with London missing out. The World Athletics Championships are heading to Africa for the first time after Kenya's capital Nairobi was confirmed as host of the 2029 edition, with London missing out. Kenya has long been a superpower in distance running but has yet to host an event of this scale. The championships will return to Germany in 2031 with Munich hosting. "We were fortunate to have four outstanding bids for 2029 and 2031, and this was not an easy decision for the council," said World Athletics president Sebastian Coe as he announced the decision following the Ultimate Championship in Hungary.
